claim: The Art Newspaper's 2026 city-by-city picks flag Musee d'Orsay's 'Renoir and Love' as reuniting its own Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette with loans from Stockholm, Washington and Boston.
quote: Renoir and Love | Musee d'Orsay (17 March-19 July)... will reunite the Musee d'Orsay's own Dance at Le moulin de la Galette with masterpieces from Stockholm, Washington, and Boston

claim: Time Out's '19 exhibitions worth travelling for in 2026' headlines 'Metamorphoses', a landmark show of 80+ Ovid-inspired masterpieces (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, Magritte) split across the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam and Galleria Borghese in Rome.
quote: Metamorphoses: A landmark exhibition bringing together 80+ masterpieces influenced by Ovid's epic poem, featuring works by Caravaggio, Rembrandt, and Magritte across two European art capitals.

claim: ArtRabbit frames the National Gallery's 'Van Eyck: The Portraits' (London, from 21 Nov 2026) as uniting all nine surviving van Eyck painted portraits for the first and only time, the defining once-in-a-generation loan show of 2026.
quote: Van Eyck: The Portraits | The National Gallery, London | all nine of Jan van Eyck's surviving painted portraits...for the first and only time

claim: ArtRabbit's blockbuster list applies once-in-a-generation / first-ever scholarship framing to Fondation Beyeler's Cezanne ('rare chance to see the late phase as a coherent argument'), Cardiff's Gwen John 150th-birthday survey, the Courtauld's first-ever Seurat seascapes show, and the National Gallery's first UK Zurbaran.
quote: Cezanne | Fondation Beyeler... 'rare chance to see the late phase as a coherent, luminous argument'... Gwen John... 'once-in-a-generation gathering for Gwen John's 150th birthday'... Seurat and the Sea... 'first-ever exhibition dedicated to Seurat's seascapes'

claim: The British Museum frames the Bayeux Tapestry loan (Sept 2026) as 'one for the ages' and the first UK display in nearly 1,000 years, forecasting up to 7.5 million visitors and insuring the textile for ~£800 million.
quote: the first time the tapestry has been displayed in the UK since it was made almost 1,000 years ago... up to 7.5 million visitors forecast to attend... director Nicholas Cullinan called it 'one for the ages'

claim: Against the hype, conservators who restored the Bayeux Tapestry advised against the London trip and a petition to Macron passed 60,000 signatures, making it 2026's clearest case where once-in-a-millennium framing collides with cautionary expert opposition.
quote: the only experts who have spoken publicly, such as Isabelle Bedat and Beatrice Girault, the restorers who worked on the tapestry between 1981 and 1983, have advised against the trip to London... petition... surpassed 60,000 signatures

claim: Apollo's preview of Fondation Beyeler's Cezanne (Basel, 25 Jan-25 May 2026) frames it as a scholarship-led survey of ~80 late oils and watercolours centred on Mont Sainte-Victoire, valued for substance rather than once-in-a-generation hype.
quote: some 80 oil paintings and watercolours from Cezanne's late period... undiminished appetite for formal experimentation and vivid use of colour... Multiple renderings of Mont Sainte-Victoire

claim: The New Statesman's 2026 preview separates substance from hype, praising Amsterdam/Rome's 'Metamorphoses' (Titian to Magritte) and 'Rothko in Florence' as 'the stuff of dreams' while flagging the Frida Kahlo and Tracey Emin shows as tests of 'whether their art actually measures up to their column inches'.
quote: Rothko in Florence... 'the stuff of dreams'... an opportunity to judge whether their art actually measures up to their column inches
